_draft: DRAFT of the plot (chapter 1 of the Voice) for review and rewriting.

chapters.title: Chapter 1: Seven, three, one, nine

fragments.text: The Voice's numbers aren't random: 7-3-1-9 repeats every hour on the hour, like a timetable.
A station calling itself Echo-7 answers on the medium band. It says its name and cuts out.

fragments.source: Police station archive or Irene's lab
fragments.text: A folder: "Project Echo. Early warning network. Activation: 03:10". The hour the Silence began.
At the northern antenna there's equipment installed after the Silence. Plate: ECHO-7. It relays something from farther away.
For the first time, the Voice asks something: "Who else is listening?"

finale: Bunker operator. Seven, three, one, nine. We know you're listening.
The Silence didn't end. It just got quieter.
When you're ready, find the Echo-7 station. End of transmission.
chapters.closing: Chapter 1 complete. The Voice knows you exist.

lines: Three knocks on the hatch. Slow. Evenly spaced.
Nobody is out there. Nobody should be.
reaction: Don't open it. Whatever it says, don't open it.

lines: The vents carry something that isn't air. A whisper, almost words. It stops when {name} gets up to listen.
reaction: It said my name. I swear it said my name.

lines: The radio switches itself on at 3:10. Static. Then, very clearly, a door closing. Then static again.
Footsteps on the ground above the bunker. They walk to the hatch. They stand there. After a long time, they walk away.
reaction: Someone was standing on top of us.

lines: The lights dim to orange for a few seconds. The generator never missed a beat. Something else drew the power.
A scratching inside the north wall, where there's only dirt. It moves along the wall, toward the bunks.
reaction: I'm sleeping by the radio tonight. Don't argue.

lines: A voice is counting under its breath in the dark. Seven, three, one, nine. When {name} turns on the light, everyone's asleep.
reaction: Which one of you was counting?

lines: The log prints a line you didn't type: OPERATOR: "stay on the channel". The timestamp is tomorrow.
The storage room is cold. Not cool: cold, breath-fog cold, in one corner. The thermometer says 21 degrees.
reaction: I'm not going back in there for the beans. Someone else go.

lines: A dog barks outside, far away. Then closer. Then right at the hatch. Then a man's voice says "good boy" and it all stops.
{name} finds a photograph taped inside a locker nobody uses: this bunker, from inside, everyone asleep. The paper is new.
reaction: Who took this? WHO TOOK THIS?

lines: The hatch wheel turns a quarter turn on its own. Then back. Like someone testing it from outside.
reaction: I'm putting the bar across it. Every night now.

lines: A lullaby hums through the water pipes, the same one from the medium band. It ends mid-note.
reaction: That's the song from the radio. How is it in the pipes?

lines: The static on every band stops at once. Total silence, for nine seconds. Then it comes back, as if nothing happened.
